**5. RESOLUTIONS**

The following resolutions were placed before the members and were carried unanimously unless otherwise noted.

**Resolution 5.1: Appointment of Auditors for the Financial Year 2025–26**

The President proposed the re-appointment of M/s Rao & Associates, Chartered Accountants, as the statutory auditors of the association for the financial year ending 31 March 2026. The proposal was seconded by Mr. Rajesh Menon and carried unanimously. The auditors have consented to the appointment, and their remuneration shall be fixed by the Managing Committee.

**Resolution 5.2: Revision of Monthly Maintenance Charges**

The Treasurer's office had circulated a proposal to revise the monthly maintenance charges with effect from 1 June 2025. After discussion, the members resolved that the monthly maintenance for all unit types be increased by 8% over the existing rates. The revised schedule of charges shall be displayed on the notice board and circulated to all members by 30 April 2025. The resolution was carried with 212 votes in favour, 14 against, and 6 abstentions.

**Resolution 5.3: Adoption of the Annual Budget for the Year 2025–26**

The proposed budget for the financial year 2025–26, as circulated along with the notice of this meeting, was taken up for consideration. The budget projects total receipts of Rs. 1,04,50,000 and total expenditure of Rs. 1,01,20,000, leaving an estimated surplus of Rs. 3,30,000. The members adopted the budget as presented. The President noted that the budget includes a provision of Rs. 12,00,000 for the replacement of the water pipelines in Blocks C and D, a matter which was discussed in detail during the meeting.

**Resolution 5.4: Approval of the Action Plan for Recovery of Outstanding Dues**

The members deliberated on the outstanding maintenance dues amounting to Rs. 4,21,350 as of 31 March 2025. The President explained that final notices had been issued to the five defaulting units and that the Managing Committee proposed to initiate recovery proceedings under Bye-Law 14(3) if the amounts were not cleared by 30 April 2025. The members approved the action plan. It was further resolved that the Managing Committee may, at its discretion, enter into a one-time settlement arrangement with any defaulter, provided that at least 50% of the outstanding amount is paid upfront and the balance is cleared within six months.

**Resolution 5.5: Installation of Solar Panels on the Clubhouse and Community Hall Roofs**

Mr. Anil Kulkarni moved a proposal to install grid-connected solar photovoltaic panels on the rooftops of the clubhouse and the community hall. The proposal, which had been examined by the Facilities Sub-Committee, estimates a capital cost of Rs. 18,50,000 and an expected payback period of five to six years. The members resolved to authorise the Managing Committee to invite tenders and to proceed with the installation, subject to the necessary approvals from the electricity department. The resolution was carried with 198 votes in favour, 22 against, and 12 abstentions.

**Resolution 5.6: Amendment to Bye-Law 11(2) Regarding Pet Ownership**

The Managing Committee had proposed an amendment to Bye-Law 11(2) to require members to register their pets with the association office and to provide proof of vaccination annually. After a brief discussion, the members approved the amendment by the requisite two-thirds majority. The amendment shall come into force on 1 May 2025, and the registration fee shall be Rs. 500 per pet per year.

**SECTION 4: ELECTION OF THE MANAGING COMMITTEE**

4.1 Composition of the Managing Committee

(a) The Managing Committee shall consist of nine (9) Members, comprising the following offices:

(i) President
(ii) Vice-President
(iii) Secretary
(iv) Joint Secretary
(v) Treasurer
(vi) Four (4) Executive Members

(b) No Member shall hold more than one office on the Managing Committee in the same term.

(c) The term of office of every Member of the Managing Committee shall be two (2) years, commencing from the date of the Annual General Meeting at which they are declared elected, and ending at the conclusion of the second succeeding Annual General Meeting.

4.2 Eligibility for Candidature

(a) Any Member who has been a Member of the Association for a continuous period of not less than two (2) years immediately preceding the date of nomination shall be eligible to contest any office.

(b) A Member who has served two (2) consecutive full terms on the Managing Committee shall be ineligible to contest the immediately succeeding election for the same office.

(c) A Member against whom disciplinary proceedings are pending under Section 10 of these Bye-laws shall not be eligible to contest any election until such proceedings are concluded.

4.3 Election Procedure

(a) The outgoing Managing Committee shall appoint an Election Officer from amongst the Members of the Association who is not a candidate in the forthcoming election.

(b) The Election Officer shall announce the schedule of elections at least thirty (30) days prior to the date of the Annual General Meeting, by affixing a notice on the notice boards of the clubhouse and the main gate, and by circulation through the official Residents' email group.

(c) Nominations shall be received in writing in the prescribed form, duly proposed by one Member and seconded by another Member, and shall be delivered to the Election Officer not later than fourteen (14) days prior to the date of the Annual General Meeting.

(d) A candidate may withdraw their candidature by written notice to the Election Officer not later than seven (7) days prior to the date of the Annual General Meeting.

(e) The Election Officer shall scrutinise all nominations and publish the final list of validly nominated candidates at least five (5) days prior to the date of the Annual General Meeting.

(f) If the number of validly nominated candidates for an office equals the number of vacancies, the candidates shall be declared elected unopposed.

(g) If the number of validly nominated candidates exceeds the number of vacancies, an election by secret ballot shall be held at the Annual General Meeting.

(h) The Election Officer shall conduct the election and shall declare the results at the Annual General Meeting itself.

(i) In the event of a tie in the number of votes cast for any office, the Election Officer shall determine the winner by drawing lots in the presence of the candidates concerned and the scrutineers.

4.4 Voting Rights

(a) Every Member present at the Annual General Meeting shall be entitled to vote.

(b) Each membership shall carry one (1) vote, irrespective of the number of joint owners.

(c) Voting by proxy shall not be permitted.

(d) Voting shall be by secret ballot in the case of contested elections. For other matters, voting may be by show of hands unless a poll is demanded by at least ten (10) Members present.

4.5 Scrutineers

(a) The Election Officer shall appoint two (2) scrutineers from amongst the Members present who are not candidates in the election.
